title: ci(publish-smoke): a cancelled smoke reports pending "nothing measured", never failure
body:
Fixes #24499
Clause-②: no

## What changed

One file, `.github/workflows/publish-smoke.yml` (+14 / -5, 19 changed lines):

- The `Report verdict to the release PR head` step now maps `job.status` with a `case`. `cancelled` writes `pending` with the description "Cancelled before a verdict (superseded by a newer smoke, timed out, or stopped by hand) — nothing measured" (106 characters; the status API caps descriptions at 140). `success` and `failure` write exactly what they wrote before. Any other value still falls through to `failure`.
- Three header lines say how to read the new entry when you walk the status history: a `pending` reading "Cancelled before a verdict" closes a run that measured nothing.

The step's `if:` (`always() && needs.resolve.outputs.report-sha != ''`), the `Mark pending` step, `resolve-guard`, the concurrency block and every other job are untouched.

## Mapping, before and after

| `job.status` in the verdict step | when it is reached | before (state · description) | after (state · description) |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `success` | every step passed | `success` · Fresh install of the release candidate: auth + CRUD green | unchanged |
| `failure` | a step failed (build, pack, install or a probe) | `failure` · Release candidate fails a fresh install — see the run log | unchanged |
| `cancelled` | cancel-in-progress supersession (all 75 measured cancellations), a job `timeout-minutes` overrun (none measured), or a manual stop | `failure` · Release candidate fails a fresh install — see the run log | `pending` · Cancelled before a verdict (superseded by a newer smoke, timed out, or stopped by hand) — nothing measured |
| `skipped` | **not reachable.** `skipped` is not a `job.status` value, and a skipped `pack-smoke` job runs no steps, so nothing is written before or after this change | — | — |
| any other value | none is documented | `failure` | `failure` (the `*)` arm keeps the fail-closed default) |

How I checked the table: I extracted the step's `run:` body from the YAML, substituted each `job.status` value, and ran it under bash with a stub `gh` that prints the `state=` and `description=` it receives. I did this at `BASE` 959ee317b and at head 0c5ad5810. The table above is that output. The probe script lives in my scratchpad; no test file is added.

## Mechanism, measured (each PM hypothesis)

1. **The step at `origin/main` 959ee317b.** Confirmed as the dispatch described it. The verdict step is at `:236`–`:249`: `if: always() && needs.resolve.outputs.report-sha != ''`, and any `job.status` other than `success` became `state=failure` with "Release candidate fails a fresh install — see the run log". The concurrency block is at `:73`–`:75`: `group: publish-smoke-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`.
2. **What happens on a cancel.**
   - GitHub's docs (`github/docs` at dae83f7d28, `content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts.md`) say: "`job.status` … Possible values are `success`, `failure`, or `cancelled`". `expressions.md` says `always()` "Causes the step to always execute … even when canceled". `workflow-syntax.md` says `jobs.JOB_ID.timeout-minutes` is "The maximum number of minutes to let a job run before GitHub automatically cancels it", so a job timeout is also a `cancelled`.
   - The REST job and step records of the two runs named on the card:
     - run 39221870768, job 117958850974: `Build` is `cancelled`, `Publish smoke (packed tarballs)` is `skipped`, and `Report verdict to the release PR head` ran and concluded `success`. The job is `cancelled`.
     - run 39222297525, job 117960447073: the same pattern.
   - The status history on `4ed16392ee` shows both runs writing `failure` (08:22:52Z and 08:24:32Z). So the `always()` step does run on a cancel, and `job.status` there is not `success`. No step failed, so of the three documented values it read `cancelled`.
   - ⛔ NOT MEASURED directly: the literal rendered value. The job logs redirect to a blob host that this container's proxy refuses (403), so I could not read the expanded script line.
   - **Ordering.** The superseding run's first job starts only after the cancelled run has ended. Run 39221870768 ended at 08:22:55Z and the `Resolve target` job of 39222297525 started at 08:22:56Z. Run 39222297525 ended at 08:24:36Z and `Resolve target` of 39222454134 started at 08:24:37Z. So a cancelled run's write always lands before the newer run's own `pending`.
3. **Route: (b) with `pending`.** The four-axis reasoning is in the next section.
4. **Parsers of this workflow.** All are green, listed under Gates. `check:workflow-status-functions` scopes job-level `if:` only, and this diff changes no `if:`.

## Route choice — (b) `pending` + "nothing measured"; not (a) silence, not `error`

**Census.** I listed the `publish-smoke.yml` runs through the REST run list (last 300, read 2026-10-19 around 08:40Z). Of these, 299 are `workflow_run` smokes created between 2026-10-16T00:25Z and 2026-10-19T08:23Z: 224 `success`, 75 `cancelled`, 0 `failure`. For every one of the 75 cancelled runs, a newer smoke was created before it ended. The longest cancelled run lasted 9.1 minutes against a 45-minute job timeout. So no timeout and no stand-alone cancel shows up in the window.

**The options and their failure modes.**

- **(a) Write nothing on a cancel.** No red, and the newer run's `pending` follows. But the cancelled run's last entry stays "Installing the release candidate into a fresh project…", which stops being true the moment the run is cancelled. Someone walking the history then has to infer "superseded" from two `pending` entries in a row. On a timeout or a manual stop with no later smoke, the head would show a false "Installing…" indefinitely.
- **(b) `error` + "nothing measured".** Never leaves a stale `pending`. However, `error` renders red, just like `failure`, and the combined status rolls it up as a failure. The window between the cancelled run's write and the newer run's `pending` is about 15 seconds both before and after this change (08:22:52Z → 08:23:08Z, 08:24:32Z → 08:24:46Z). So `error` keeps the exact red flash the maintainer escalated, on about a quarter of all smokes. Only the wording would change.
- **(b) `pending` + "nothing measured" (chosen).** No red on a supersession. The cancelled run closes its own entry in words, so the history explains itself. Its stale case is bounded:
  - It needs a cancel that is not a supersession (timeout or manual stop, 0 of 75 measured) and also no later Release run before the head merges. Every push to `main` starts a Release run, and that run starts a new smoke on the open release PR.
  - Even then the head reads an honest `pending` that says "nothing measured". That is never green, and it never claims a measurement.

**Four axes.**

- **实际业务需求 (real business need).** The scenario that actually occurs is supersession: 75 of 299 smokes, every cancel in the window. That is the case the maintainer hit on #24477. A timeout or manual cancel has zero measured occurrences, so the route is chosen for the observed case and only kept honest for the others.
- **项目长远合理性 (long-term soundness).** Every run now closes its own entry in the status history with a truthful state, which matches "absence must be loud". The fix stays one `case` with no new job and no extra API call. I rejected discriminating supersession from a timeout at run time (for example by looking up newer runs during the cancel): it adds machinery and new failure modes, and nothing measured asks for it.
- **防 AI 写错 (keep AI from getting it wrong).** This card was itself filed from a history walk that read `failure` entries. With the change, `failure` stays reserved for a smoke that ran and failed (plus `resolve-guard`'s self-describing "never smoked", unchanged). A cancelled run says so in words, and the combined status never reads red for a run that measured nothing. With `error`, a rollup reader would see red again; with silence, a reader has to know an inference rule.
- **创业阶段不扩散 (no scope sprawl at this stage).** No new gate, job or required check, and one file. A cancelled run makes one extra status write, about 75 over 3.5 days.

## Wanted / Done when — conclusions

- **Wanted 1.** A smoke that did not reach a verdict writes no verdict. Done: `cancelled` maps to `pending` "Cancelled before a verdict … — nothing measured" and never to `failure`.
- **Wanted 2.** A genuinely failing smoke keeps writing `failure` exactly as today, and `resolve-guard`'s explicit red stays. Done: the `failure` arm is byte-identical in state and description, and `resolve-guard` is not in the diff.
- **Wanted 3.** No new gate, no required-check change, Tier H draft. Done: the PR is a draft and stays one for an authorised approval.
- **Done when 1.** See the mapping table above (`skipped` is covered as unreachable).
- **Done when 2.** The PR names the expected reading of the next superseded smoke (this paragraph) and the seat records the first reading on `main` after the merge.
  - The PR's own CI cannot exercise this. A `workflow_run` workflow runs the file on the default branch, and the dispatch rules out dispatching it. The first reading therefore comes after the merge.
  - Expected status history on the release PR head:
    1. run A: `pending` "Installing the release candidate into a fresh project…";
    2. run A: `pending` "Cancelled before a verdict (superseded by a newer smoke, timed out, or stopped by hand) — nothing measured", linking run A, which concludes `cancelled`;
    3. run B: `pending` "Installing…";
    4. run B: `success` or `failure`.
  - No `failure` "fails a fresh install" may come from a run that concluded `cancelled`. The seat records the first such reading (run id and status history).
- **Done when 3.** Run 39222454134, in flight at filing, concluded **`success`** (REST run record), so there is no candidate failure to split off and no separate card.

## Acceptance notes

- **Timeout loudness changes direction.** A job that overruns its 45-minute `timeout-minutes` is a `cancelled` job (docs above). It used to read red `failure` "fails a fresh install" and now reads `pending` "Cancelled before a verdict … timed out …". No such run appears among the 299 measured. Making a hung smoke read red would be separate work; carrier: none (承接者:无).
- **Bounded stale pending.** If a cancel is not followed by any later smoke before the release PR merges (a timeout or manual stop, then no push to `main`), the head keeps the honest `pending` above. It is not red and not green. A re-run of the smoke or the next Release run replaces it.
- **`origin/main` moved after `BASE`.** It advanced to 7e58e0a27 (a `packages/cli` test budget only), which is disjoint from this file, so I did not merge it. The PR's merge ref and the queue cover it.

## Gates

Derivation: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, run with no paths. It read the change set from git against merge base 959ee317b: 1 path, 19 changed lines. It listed 39 commands: 31 matched by path and 8 that run on every change.

Local run at head **0c5ad5810** (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`). Every command's output went to its own log, and the exit code was captured before any pipe. **All 39 exited 0:**

- **Direct node scripts (17):**
  - `check-aggregator-roster.mjs` and `--self-test`
  - `check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs` and `--self-test`
  - `check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs`
  - `check-position-name-fold-loaders.mjs` and `--self-test`
  - `check-self-test-wired.mjs` and `--self-test`
  - `check-self-test-workflow-commands.mjs` and `--self-test`
  - `check-step-collectors.mjs` and `--self-test`
  - `check-whole-set-label-write.mjs` and `--self-test`
  - `docs-audit/check-drift-comment.mjs`
  - `pm/ci-failure.mjs --self-test`
- **pnpm gates (22):**
  - `check:agent-test-spelling`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:declared-population-live`, `check:driver-memory-census`
  - `check:gitlink-declared`, `check:node-version`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:pm-dispatch-gates` (fast tier, 1913 cases)
  - `check:pm-expected-skips`, `check:pm-governed-merges`, `check:pm-post-stamped`, `check:pm-record-recognisers`
  - `check:pnpm-acquisition`, `check:pnpm-filter-targets`, `check:refd-timer-probe`, `check:required-contexts`
  - `check:shard-attestation`, `check:stall-guard-budget`, `check:stall-guard-headroom`, `check:watch-hint-literal`
  - `check:workflow-status-functions`, `check:workflow-step-name-quoting`

Verdict lines:

- `check-workflow-status-functions: OK (scanned 40 workflow file(s), 75 job(s), 32 job-level if: expression(s); 11 read needs.*.outputs.*, all naming a status function).`
- `check-workflow-step-name-quoting: OK (scanned 40 workflow file(s) + 2 composite action file(s), 841 step name(s) …)`

Reconciliation: `--ran` with `command :: exit N` lines printed `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 39 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 39 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 39 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).`

NOT MEASURED, by value: six families take their argv or `env:` from a CI run and have no local invocation. They are `check-required-contexts.mjs --verify-required-set` and five `check-shard-attestation.mjs --emit/--verify` forms. CI owns them, along with the full farm.

No package is touched, so no build closure and no package tests were needed. No changeset: a workflow file publishes nothing, so the PR carries `skip-changeset`.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么**:发布冒烟(publish-smoke)被新一轮冒烟取代而取消时,不再往 Version Packages PR 上写红色 `failure`「候选版本全新安装失败」,改为写黄色 `pending`「在得出结论前被取消 —— 什么都没测」。真正失败的冒烟照旧写 `failure`,成功照旧写 `success`。只改了一个文件,19 行。

**为什么改**:#24477 上那个让人以为「ci 崩了」的红叉,就是被取消的冒烟误报出来的。每次合并到 main 都会触发新一轮 Release 和新一轮冒烟,旧的那轮随即被取消。10/16 以来的 299 次冒烟中有 75 次是这样被取消的,真失败 0 次。

**风险与代价(含回滚)**:
- 冒烟超时(45 分钟)或被手动取消、且之后再没有新冒烟时,PR 上会一直停在黄色 `pending`(文字如实写明「什么都没测」),不会变红。实测 299 次中超时 0 次。
- 本 PR 自己的 CI 跑不到这段逻辑(`workflow_run` 只读 main 上的 workflow 文件),要等合并后第一次被取代的冒烟才能看到效果,席位会记录那次读数。
- 回滚:revert 这一个提交即可。

**席位意见**:

**你要做的**:审阅并批准(`.github/workflows/**` 属 Tier H,需要你的批准)。合并后无需其他操作。
